title: The MDX portability scan autolink angle brackets: hazard or not? (design question)
description:
Filed from LCLI-697 (gap 2). An autolink such as <https://x/> exposes only the inner URL as an mdast text node, so the < and > that MDX would parse are never seen by mdxHazardFindings; the LCLI-663 review probe confirmed it was not caught.

DECIDED by opum-doc DEC-172 (4at), 2026-10-11T18:54Z: the MDX hazard scan FLAGS an angle-bracket autolink <https://...>, with the remedy naming the portable forms (use [text](url) or a bare URL); a bare URL and a [text](url) link are NOT flagged. Measured: @mdx-js/mdx 3.1.1 compile throws on the autolink form, while the bare and [x](url) forms compile.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The MDX portability scan FLAGS an angle-bracket autolink such as <https://x.example/>, and the finding remedy names the portable forms: use [text](url) or a bare URL.
Check: the scan does NOT flag a bare URL or a [text](url) link, so the new arm cannot over-trigger (positive control).
Tests pin both directions: the autolink is flagged; a bare URL and a [text](url) link are not.

implementationNotes:
DEC-172 (4at) decided the filing's open question: the scan flags an angle-bracket autolink; a bare URL and [text](url) are not. Implemented in src/core/check.ts: mdxHazardFindings gained a `link` arm — a link node whose SOURCE begins with `<` (an autolink) is flagged, while a `[text](url)` link's source begins with `[` and a bare URL stays a `text` node under the plain CommonMark parser the scan uses. The new autolinkHazard message names the portable forms (use [text](url) or a bare URL); docs/reference/portable-markdown.md's MDX-hazards list gains the autolink. Tests in test/check.test.ts ("checkBundle — MDX hazards") pin both directions plus the email-autolink case. Gates: bun run lint, bun run typecheck, bun test (5003 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail) and bun run lore check (exit 0) all green.

Observation (not fixed; outside this task's scope): the new arm surfaces three pre-existing angle-bracket autolinks in the repository's own docs — docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md (two) and docs/stories/prepare-the-first-lore-cli-release.md (one) — as portability warnings. They are warnings, the docs gate still exits 0.

Review round 1 (review-assignment on 669db1ef, changes-requested) — all four findings addressed:
- (major) docs/reference/portable-markdown.md's MDX-safety remedy gave only "escape or fence raw < and {", whose escape half breaks an autolink. Added a second rule: rewrite an angle-bracket autolink (bare URL or [text](url)), never escape it.
- (major) no CHANGELOG entry for the new portability rule; added an [Unreleased] ### Changed bullet.
- (minor) the repository's own docs emitted the new warning at three sites. Fixed the two in docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md (angle brackets dropped to bare URLs). The third, in docs/stories/prepare-the-first-lore-cli-release.md, sits inside a `lore:tasks` managed block regenerated from LCLI-327's title — a Done record — so it is left as written (detection, not conversion; a Done record is not rewritten), and `lore check` still exits 0 on it.
- (minor) an autolink whose URL contains `{` produced two findings (the autolink arm plus the text-node raw-`{` arm). The raw-character arms now skip a text node an angle-bracket autolink covers, so one finding per construct — consistent with a `[text](url)` destination, whose URL text is not scanned either. Pinned by a new test.

Round-1 revision: 669db1ef. Gates re-run green after the fixes: bun run lint, bun run typecheck, bun test (5004 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail), bun run lore check (exit 0, now 1 autolink warning — the managed-block site — plus the pre-existing capacity warning).

Review round 2 (review-assignment on c314269a, changes-requested) — findings addressed: (major) the autolink remedy bullet in docs/reference/portable-markdown.md over-claimed that a bare URL "renders everywhere the angle-bracket form does"; a bare URL autolinks only where GFM autolink literals render (GitHub, Obsidian) and is plain text in the scaffolded MkDocs/Material config (no autolink extension), so the bullet now names [text](url) as the portable form and states the bare-URL limit. (minor) docs/reference/cli-surface.md's parallel portability-lint enumeration gains angle-bracket autolinks. (minor) the finalSummary's test count is refreshed to 5004. The reviewer CLEARED the mechanism, the warning-tier/exit-0 behaviour, the positive control, and the residual managed-block warning.
finalSummary: Implemented DEC-172 (4at): the MDX portability scan now flags an angle-bracket autolink (<https://...>), naming the portable rewrite (a [text](url) link or a bare URL), while a bare URL and [text](url) stay unflagged. src/core/check.ts mdxHazardFindings gains a link-node arm keyed on the node's SOURCE starting with '<', and a < or { inside an autolink's own URL is reported once, with the autolink. docs/reference/portable-markdown.md's MDX-safety rules gain the autolink remedy (rewrite, not escape) and its hazard list, cli-surface.md's portability-lint enumeration and CHANGELOG.md record it. test/check.test.ts pins both directions plus the email-autolink and URL-inner cases. Gates green: lint, typecheck, bun test (5004 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail), bun run lore check (exit 0). Delivered under opum-control job-1hocc8w.
